title: McDonald critères pour multiple Sclerosis (2017 Revision)
formula:
**McDonald Criteria (2017):**

| Clinical attacks* | Number of lesions with objective clinical evidence** | Additional data needed for diagnosis of MS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ≥2 | ≥2 | No additional tests required to demonstrate dissemination in space and time |
| 1 (as well as clear-cut historical evidence of a previous attack involving a lesion in a distinct anatomical location) | No additional tests required to demonstrate dissemination in space and time | |
| 1 | Dissemination in space demonstrated by an additional clinical attack implicating a different CNS site or by MRI | |
| 1 | ≥2 | Dissemination in time demonstrated by additional clinical attack or MRI, or presence of CSF-specific oligoclonal bands |
| 1 | Dissemination in space demonstrated by an additional clinical attack implicating a different CNS site or by MRI and dissemination in time demonstrated by additional clinical attack or MRI, or presence of CSF-specific oligoclonal bands | |

*“Clinical attack” = monophasic clinical episode with patient-reported symptoms and objective findings reflecting inflammatory demyelinating CNS event (focal or multifocal), subacute or acute, for ≥24 hrs, with or without recovery, and no fever or infection present. Attack, relapse, exacerbation, and clinically isolated syndrome (first episode) are all synonymous.

**“Objective clinical evidence” = abnormality on neurologic exam, imaging (MRI or optical coherence tomography), or visual evoked potentials, corresponding to anatomical location suggested by symptoms.

how_to_use.when: Patients chez qui une SEP est suspectée et qui ont bénéficié d’une IRM.
how_to_use.pearls:
- Développé pour les patients présentant un syndrome cliniquement isolé typique, chez qui d’autres diagnostics sont jugés improbables, et NON pour différencier la SEP d’autres affections.
- Ces critères peuvent aider à différencier la SEP rémittente d’autres syndromes cliniquement isolés qui peuvent la mimer.

next_steps.advice: Le seuil pour des examens complémentaires (c.-à-d., IRM de la moelle épinière ou examen du LCR) doit être bas, selon le panel international qui a élaboré ces critères.
